course_map.title: Signed distance to a plane
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compute a signed plane coordinate along a path
course_map.assessment_target: Compute a signed plane coordinate along a path

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: For a fixed plane family define unit normal n, fixed origin o, positive spacing d and indexed sheets n dot(x-o)=k d. Signed distance to sheet k is s_k=n dot(x-o)-k d; dimensionless phase is q=n dot(x-o)/d. A nonunit normal needs explicit normalization.

worked_example.task_and_answer: n=(3/5,4/5,0), o=0,d=3/5m,x(t)=(2t,0,0)m with t in seconds. n dot n=1, s0=6t/5m and q=2t. At t=1/4s, s0=3/10m,q=1/2; at t=1/2s the k=1 sheet is reached.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Use x(t)=(-2t,0,0)m with the same fixed origin and spacing. At t=1/2s, q=-1 and s_(-1)=0. If the origin is deliberately redefined as(1,0,0)m, q shifts by-1; retain that separate origin contract rather than moving it while comparing events.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A negative q is not an invalid distance; it records direction and sheet label. Do not change d or o to fit a preferred event. d=0 is undefined and requires a retained failure status.

course_map.title: Crossing rates from velocity
course_map.worked_example_capability: Derive the projected crossing rate with dimensions
course_map.assessment_target: Derive the projected crossing rate with dimensions

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Differentiate q for fixed n,o,d: qdot=n dot v/d in signed crossings per second. The magnitude is an unsigned rate. A time-varying n,o,d needs qdot=(ndot dot(x-o)+n dot(v-odot))/d-q*ddot/d, with each input specified.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For n=(3/5,4/5,0),v=(2,0,0)m/s,d=3/5m, n dot v=6/5m/s and qdot=2s^-1. With v=(-2,0,0), qdot=-2s^-1; both have unsigned frequency2Hz but opposite sheet order.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For n=(0,1,0),v=(2,0,0),d=1m, qdot=0 and no traversal period exists. For v=(0,-3,0)m/s, qdot=-3s^-1 and magnitude period1/3s.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A zero rate gives no finite crossing period, not an event every zero seconds. Absolute value must not replace the original signed rate. The fixed-plane derivative is invalid for moving planes unless all derivative terms vanish.

course_map.title: Spatial spacing and a temporal signal
course_map.worked_example_capability: Convert a spatial ruler into a time scale
course_map.assessment_target: Convert a spatial ruler into a time scale

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Convert a spatial ruler to a temporal passage scale using T=d/abs(n dot v) when the projected velocity is nonzero and constant. A changing projected speed requires integrated phase, not one average frequency. Teach phase in cycles versus radians: phi=2pi q.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For d=3/5m and projected speed6/5m/s, T=1/2s. The constant trajectory meets k=0,1,2,3 at0,1/2,1,3/2s. Reversing velocity meets indices0,-1,-2,-3 at the same elapsed times.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Keeping projected speed6/5m/s but declaring a separate ruler d=6/5m doubles T to1s and halves |qdot| to1Hz. This is a new ruler contract; do not replace the original ledger. For q=2t, phi=4pi t radians.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Spatial frequency1/d, signed passage rate and angular frequency have different units. A tangent instant can have zero rate while the path still touches a sheet; the full phase path determines the event.

course_map.title: Optical, oscillator, and crystal rulers
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compare source-defined rulers without equating their physical roles
course_map.assessment_target: Compare source-defined rulers without equating their physical roles

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Read T10 ruler semantics: optical wavelength, oscillator period and matter crystal spacing are different inputs. A period is not a length without a declared propagation or motion speed. A difference/beat frequency requires two defined frequencies in one time convention.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic projected speed2m/s with optical ruler0.5m gives4 signed passages/s; a crystal ruler0.25m gives8/s. A separate oscillator period0.5s gives2Hz. Comparing magnitudes4Hz and2Hz gives a2Hz difference under a declared comparison rule, not an established optical detector beat.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: An oscillator period1/4s gives4Hz. With an expressly supplied propagation speed3m/s its propagation wavelength is3/4m; do not use the sensor speed as that propagation speed. Reversing sensor motion negates spatial passage rates while the positive oscillator frequency remains4Hz.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A numeric equality of rates does not identify light, oscillator and crystal mechanisms. No THz-to-baseband transfer follows from time averaging alone; retain ruler identity, speed definition and detector transfer inputs.

course_map.title: Events and interpolation
course_map.worked_example_capability: Locate a crossing inside a continuous bracket
course_map.assessment_target: Locate a crossing inside a continuous bracket

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: A continuous signed function with opposite-sign endpoints has at least one zero. Linear interpolation is exact only for a declared linear segment. Teach bracket retention, continuity requirements, multiple roots and tangent contacts before classifying events.

worked_example.task_and_answer: s(0)=-2/5m,s(2)=6/5m with linear s gives t*=0-(-2/5)*2/(8/5)=1/2s. Retain bracket[0,2]s and both endpoints. For s=(t-1)(t-2), the endpoints t0 and3 are both positive but zeros occur at1 and2; endpoint signs alone miss them.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For linear s(1)=-1m,s(3)=3m, the root is3/2s. For s=(t-1)^2, t=1 is a contact with derivative0 and no sign reversal. For a step from-1 to+1 at t=1, a sign change does not prove any zero because continuity fails.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Unknown values across a gap remain an unresolved interval. Record contacts separately from transverse passages, retain every root and bracket, and never infer absence from equal endpoint signs. Refinement changes uncertainty, not the original samples.

course_map.title: Meridian events versus spatial-sheet passages
course_map.worked_example_capability: Distinguish the different celestial and geometric event definitions
course_map.assessment_target: Distinguish the different celestial and geometric event definitions

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define celestial meridian events using an unwrapped hour angle H=LST-RA: upper meridian H=0 mod2pi, lower meridian H=pi mod2pi; quadratures are plus/minus pi/2. Define spatial-sheet events by q=k. These are different equations even when times coincide.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic H(t)=(pi/2)t with t in hours has upper transit t=0, lower transit t=2 and quadrature t=1. A separate spatial q(t)=t-1/2 crosses k=0 at t=1/2. No meridian event is implied at that spatial crossing.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For H(t)=pi(t-1) radians with t in hours, upper transit occurs at t=1 and lower at t=0 or2. For q(t)=2t, sheet k=1 occurs at1/2h. Label event type, normal or celestial object, clock and branch on each row.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: RA wrap at24h can create a numerical jump unless unwrapped; it is not a physical transit. Celestial direction crossing, meridian passage and a sensor crossing a spatial sheet must not share one unlabeled event field.

course_map.title: A signed crossing ledger
course_map.worked_example_capability: Retain direction, polarity, uncertainty, gaps, and event provenance
course_map.assessment_target: Retain direction, polarity, uncertainty, gaps, and event provenance

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Build one row per event candidate with family/sheet, fixed geometry, epoch/time, signed direction, normal orientation, bracket, continuity/interpolation rule, contact/pass classification, raw-source reference and any uncertainty/gap. A missing interval is a row, not an omission.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For x=(2t,0,0), family A n=(3/5,4/5,0),d=3/5m has events k=0..3 at0,1/2,1,3/2s, direction+. Add family B n=(1,0,0),d=2m with k=0,1 at0,1s. Coincident t=1 events retain both family IDs; they are not duplicate measurements.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Reverse x and list A indices0,-1,-2,-3 at the same times with direction-. Include the tangent t=1 and the unresolved gap(1,2)s from a separate example with their distinct statuses. Reconstruct every known signed distance at bracket endpoints from the saved path and geometry.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Polarity is a separately declared orientation/sign convention; it is not inferred by sorting times. Keep uncertain, zero-rate and contact rows. A ledger with only successful positive passages loses information.

source_scope.plane_contract: Unit normal, fixed origin and positive spacing are explicit. q=n dot(x-o)/d; signed qdot preserves direction. Moving n,o,d require the full derivative. Magnitudes are used only for specified unsigned rates.
source_scope.event_contract: Continuity plus sign change proves at least one root; not uniqueness. Multiple roots, tangencies, discontinuities, endpoints, missing intervals and failed refinements remain in the ledger. Linear interpolation is exact only for a declared linear segment.
source_scope.rulers: Optical wavelength, oscillator period and crystal spacing retain distinct physical meanings. Any period-to-length or baseband conversion needs explicitly supplied speed/transfer inputs.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: For a fixed plane family define unit normal n, fixed origin o, positive spacing d and indexed sheets n dot(x-o)=k d. Signed distance to sheet k is s_k=n dot(x-o)-k d; dimensionless phase is q=n dot(x-o)/d. A nonunit normal needs explicit normalization.

worked_example.task_and_answer: n=(3/5,4/5,0), o=0,d=3/5m,x(t)=(2t,0,0)m with t in seconds. n dot n=1, s0=6t/5m and q=2t. At t=1/4s, s0=3/10m,q=1/2; at t=1/2s the k=1 sheet is reached.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Use x(t)=(-2t,0,0)m with the same fixed origin and spacing. At t=1/2s, q=-1 and s_(-1)=0. If the origin is deliberately redefined as(1,0,0)m, q shifts by-1; retain that separate origin contract rather than moving it while comparing events.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A negative q is not an invalid distance; it records direction and sheet label. Do not change d or o to fit a preferred event. d=0 is undefined and requires a retained failure status.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Differentiate q for fixed n,o,d: qdot=n dot v/d in signed crossings per second. The magnitude is an unsigned rate. A time-varying n,o,d needs qdot=(ndot dot(x-o)+n dot(v-odot))/d-q*ddot/d, with each input specified.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For n=(3/5,4/5,0),v=(2,0,0)m/s,d=3/5m, n dot v=6/5m/s and qdot=2s^-1. With v=(-2,0,0), qdot=-2s^-1; both have unsigned frequency2Hz but opposite sheet order.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For n=(0,1,0),v=(2,0,0),d=1m, qdot=0 and no traversal period exists. For v=(0,-3,0)m/s, qdot=-3s^-1 and magnitude period1/3s.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A zero rate gives no finite crossing period, not an event every zero seconds. Absolute value must not replace the original signed rate. The fixed-plane derivative is invalid for moving planes unless all derivative terms vanish.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Convert a spatial ruler to a temporal passage scale using T=d/abs(n dot v) when the projected velocity is nonzero and constant. A changing projected speed requires integrated phase, not one average frequency. Teach phase in cycles versus radians: phi=2pi q.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For d=3/5m and projected speed6/5m/s, T=1/2s. The constant trajectory meets k=0,1,2,3 at0,1/2,1,3/2s. Reversing velocity meets indices0,-1,-2,-3 at the same elapsed times.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Keeping projected speed6/5m/s but declaring a separate ruler d=6/5m doubles T to1s and halves |qdot| to1Hz. This is a new ruler contract; do not replace the original ledger. For q=2t, phi=4pi t radians.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Spatial frequency1/d, signed passage rate and angular frequency have different units. A tangent instant can have zero rate while the path still touches a sheet; the full phase path determines the event.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Read T10 ruler semantics: optical wavelength, oscillator period and matter crystal spacing are different inputs. A period is not a length without a declared propagation or motion speed. A difference/beat frequency requires two defined frequencies in one time convention.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic projected speed2m/s with optical ruler0.5m gives4 signed passages/s; a crystal ruler0.25m gives8/s. A separate oscillator period0.5s gives2Hz. Comparing magnitudes4Hz and2Hz gives a2Hz difference under a declared comparison rule, not an established optical detector beat.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: An oscillator period1/4s gives4Hz. With an expressly supplied propagation speed3m/s its propagation wavelength is3/4m; do not use the sensor speed as that propagation speed. Reversing sensor motion negates spatial passage rates while the positive oscillator frequency remains4Hz.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A numeric equality of rates does not identify light, oscillator and crystal mechanisms. No THz-to-baseband transfer follows from time averaging alone; retain ruler identity, speed definition and detector transfer inputs.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: A continuous signed function with opposite-sign endpoints has at least one zero. Linear interpolation is exact only for a declared linear segment. Teach bracket retention, continuity requirements, multiple roots and tangent contacts before classifying events.

worked_example.task_and_answer: s(0)=-2/5m,s(2)=6/5m with linear s gives t*=0-(-2/5)*2/(8/5)=1/2s. Retain bracket[0,2]s and both endpoints. For s=(t-1)(t-2), the endpoints t0 and3 are both positive but zeros occur at1 and2; endpoint signs alone miss them.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For linear s(1)=-1m,s(3)=3m, the root is3/2s. For s=(t-1)^2, t=1 is a contact with derivative0 and no sign reversal. For a step from-1 to+1 at t=1, a sign change does not prove any zero because continuity fails.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Unknown values across a gap remain an unresolved interval. Record contacts separately from transverse passages, retain every root and bracket, and never infer absence from equal endpoint signs. Refinement changes uncertainty, not the original samples.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Define celestial meridian events using an unwrapped hour angle H=LST-RA: upper meridian H=0 mod2pi, lower meridian H=pi mod2pi; quadratures are plus/minus pi/2. Define spatial-sheet events by q=k. These are different equations even when times coincide.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic H(t)=(pi/2)t with t in hours has upper transit t=0, lower transit t=2 and quadrature t=1. A separate spatial q(t)=t-1/2 crosses k=0 at t=1/2. No meridian event is implied at that spatial crossing.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For H(t)=pi(t-1) radians with t in hours, upper transit occurs at t=1 and lower at t=0 or2. For q(t)=2t, sheet k=1 occurs at1/2h. Label event type, normal or celestial object, clock and branch on each row.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: RA wrap at24h can create a numerical jump unless unwrapped; it is not a physical transit. Celestial direction crossing, meridian passage and a sensor crossing a spatial sheet must not share one unlabeled event field.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Build one row per event candidate with family/sheet, fixed geometry, epoch/time, signed direction, normal orientation, bracket, continuity/interpolation rule, contact/pass classification, raw-source reference and any uncertainty/gap. A missing interval is a row, not an omission.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For x=(2t,0,0), family A n=(3/5,4/5,0),d=3/5m has events k=0..3 at0,1/2,1,3/2s, direction+. Add family B n=(1,0,0),d=2m with k=0,1 at0,1s. Coincident t=1 events retain both family IDs; they are not duplicate measurements.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Reverse x and list A indices0,-1,-2,-3 at the same times with direction-. Include the tangent t=1 and the unresolved gap(1,2)s from a separate example with their distinct statuses. Reconstruct every known signed distance at bracket endpoints from the saved path and geometry.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Polarity is a separately declared orientation/sign convention; it is not inferred by sorting times. Keep uncertain, zero-rate and contact rows. A ledger with only successful positive passages loses information.
